items.longBusinessSummary: Lumentum Holdings Inc. manufactures and sells optical and photonic products in the Americas, the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. It offers component products, including semiconductor laser chips, laser sub-assemblies, line subsystems, and wavelength management systems. The company also offers system products, such as optical modules, optical circuit switches, and industrial lasers, including short-pulse solid-state lasers and kilowatt-class fiber lasers. Its products and solutions are used in cloud, artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML), telecommunications, consumer, and industrial end-market applications. The company was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

Item 1.01.
Entry Into a Material Definitive Agreement. The Merger On November 1, 2026, Lumentum Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Lumentum” or the “Company”), entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) with Marvell Technology, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Marvell”), Java Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“Merger Sub I”) and Java Merger Sub II, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“Merger Sub II” and together with Merger Sub I, each a “Merger Sub” and collectively the “Merger Subs”). Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub I will merge with and into Lumentum (the “First Merger”), with Lumentum continuing as the surviving corporation (the “Surviving Corporation”) and as a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell, and promptly following the Effective Time (as defined below), the Surviving Corporation will merge with and into Merger Sub II (the “Second Merger” and, collectively or in seriatim with the First Merger, as applicable, the “Merger”), with Merger Sub II continuing as the surviving corporation of the Second Merger (the “Second Surviving Corporation”). The board of directors of Lumentum (the “Lumentum Board”) has unanimously: (i) approved and declared advisable the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Merger, (ii) determined that the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the Merger, are fair to, and in the best interests of, Lumentum and its stockholders, and (iii) resolved to recommend that Lumentum’s stockholders adopt the Merger Agreement. Merger Consideration At the effective time of the First Merger (the “Effective Time”), each share of common stock, par value $0.001 per share, of Lumentum (the “Lumentum Common Stock”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive 4.500 shares of common stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the “Marvell Common Stock,” and such ratio, the “Exchange Ratio”),with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common Stock payable in accordance with the Merger Agreement (the “Common Stock Merger Consideration”). At the Effective Time, each share of preferred stock, par value $0.001 per share, of Lumentum designated as Series A Convertible Preferred Stock (the “Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock” and, together with the Lumentum Common Stock, the “Lumentum Capital Stock”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive a number of shares of Marvell Common Stock equal to the product of (a) the number of shares of Lumentum Common Stock into which such share of Lumentum Preferred Stock is convertible pursuant to its terms as of immediately prior to the Effective Time and (b) the Exchange Ratio, with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common Stock payable in accordance with the Merger Agreement (the “Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration”). However, if a holder of shares of Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock makes an election in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement to receive the Merger Consideration in the form of Series B Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the “Marvell Series B Preferred Stock,” and such election, a “Preferred Stock Election”), then each share of Lumentum Preferred Stock that is held by such holder immediately prior to the Effective Time will instead be converted into the right to receive one share of Marvell Series B Preferred Stock (the “Series B Preferred Stock Merger Consideration” and together with the Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration and the Common Stock Merger Consideration, the “Merger Consideration”). The Marvell Series B Preferred Stock is intended to have the same terms and rights as the Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock, except that each share is convertible for the Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration. The shares of Marvell Common Stock to be issued in connection with the Merger will be listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (“Nasdaq”). In connection with the issuance of the Merger Consideration by Marvell, as promptly as reasonably practicable following the date of the Merger Agreement, Marvell and Lumentum will jointly prepare and cause to be filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) a registration statement on Form S-4 (the “Form S-4”), which will include the joint proxy statement of Marvell and Lumentum for their respective meetings of stockholders relating to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement.

Treatment of Equity Awards Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, each Lumentum equity award, consisting of stock options, restricted stock units and performance stock units, that is outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time will be converted into an equivalent Marvell equity award, including with respect to vesting conditions (including termination protection and provisions, expiration and post-termination exercisability), except that performance stock units will be converted into solely time-vesting restricted stock units. The number of shares of Marvell Common Stock subject to each converted equity award will be equal to the number of shares of Lumentum Common Stock then subject to the award (with the number of shares subject to any performance stock unit determined based on (i) the greater of target and actual performance levels for stock price performance metrics and (ii) except as otherwise provided by the terms of the Company’s Change in Control and Severance Benefits Plan, as amended and restated, that would apply assuming a participant’s qualifying termination of employment upon the consummation of the Merger, at projected actual performance for all other performance metrics measured through the Effective Time), multiplied by the Exchange Ratio, and the exercise price of each converted stock option will be equal to the exercise price of the Lumentum stock option divided by the Exchange Ratio. Notwithstanding the foregoing, each restricted stock unit of Lumentum that is outstanding and held by a non-employee director as of immediately prior to the Effective Time will instead be cancelled and converted into the right to receive the Common Stock Merger Consideration. Post-Closing Governance Effective as of immediately following the Effective Time, Marvell will appoint three (3) individuals designated by Lumentum from among the members of the Lumentum board of directors and reasonably acceptable to Marvell to the Marvell Board, and Marvell will nominate each such designee who is still serving for election at Marvell’s first annual meeting of stockholders following the Effective Time. Representations, Warranties and Covenants The Merger Agreement contains customary representations and warranties of Marvell and Lumentum relating to their respective businesses. Additionally, the Merger Agreement provides for customary pre-closing covenants of each of Marvell and Lumentum, including (a) subject to certain exceptions, to conduct their respective businesses in the ordinary course; (b) to cooperate and use reasonable best efforts to obtain required regulatory approvals; (c) unless the Merger Agreement is terminated in accordance with its terms, to hold a meeting of their respective stockholders to seek the requisite stockholder approvals; (d) not to solicit proposals relating to certain alternative transactions from third parties, including alternative acquisitions or business combination transactions involving Marvell or Lumentum, as applicable (an  ...

Title: Marvell Stocks Decline 6.8% With Lumentum Deal Putting Dilution Ahead of Synergies
Author: Khac Phu Nguyen   Mon, November 2, 2026 at 7:54 PM GMT+1 1 min read
Published: 2026-11-02T18:54:01+00:00
=== BODY ===
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Marvell (NASDAQ:MRVL), the custom-chip and data-center connectivity supplier, fell 6.82% to $183 at 10:05 a.m. ET on November 2 as its proposed Lumentum acquisition put dilution front and center. The proposed combination would expand Marvell's reach in optical connectivity for AI data centers. But a bigger business must deliver more earnings per share to give existing investors a compelling payoff.
Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with MRVL.
Is MRVL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.
The November 2 agreement values Lumentum at $115 billion including debt, with holders receiving 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share. Existing Marvell owners would hold approximately 67% of the combined company. Management expects the transaction to lift adjusted earnings per share in the first year after closing and projects more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost savings. Closing is expected in the first half of 2028, leaving a lengthy stretch before those promises face their delivery test.
The valuation leaves little room for disappointment. GuruFocus shows an 81/100 GF Score, with growth the strongest dimension and GF Value the weakest; a price-to-earnings ratio of 60.26 adds pressure to execute. A shareholder owning 1% of Marvell would own roughly 0.67% of the enlarged company, before other ownership changes. That smaller percentage could still represent greater economic value if Lumentum brings enough earnings and assets. Approvals, integration spending and delivery of the projected savings could determine whether this AI expansion earns its price.

Title: Micron Falls 4% as Kioxia’s Cautious Outlook Hits Memory Stocks; Western Digital Drops 5%, SanDisk Slides 3%
Author: David Moadel   Mon, November 2, 2026 at 7:53 PM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-11-02T18:53:55+00:00
=== BODY ===
Kioxia's below-estimate December-quarter guidance sent Micron down 4% and Western Digital down 5%, extending both stocks' month-long losses past 20%.
Citrini analyst Jukan read Lumentum's sale to Marvell as a signal management expects the AI cycle to collapse within two to three years.
Kioxia CFO Kawamura called the soft outlook a shipment timing issue, saying AI demand stays robust and next year's output is already sold out.
Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Micron Technology didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat MU. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.
A cautious forecast from Kioxia Holdings, Japan's largest memory chipmaker, turned an overnight gain in Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) into a loss and pulled memory stocks lower. Micron stock is at $853.34, down 4% this afternoon. The decline adds to a pullback from an AI-fueled run in the chipmaker's shares.
Over the past month, Micron stock is down 20%. That slide comes despite record results: on September 30, the company reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $54.23 billion, up 379.3% year over year, with an adjusted gross margin of 87%. For Q1 FY2027, Micron forecast its revenue to $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion.
Kioxia Holdings guided its December-quarter operating profit to 2 trillion yen, the company said on November 2. That forecast stands only slightly above the 1.99 trillion yen Kioxia earned in the September quarter, and it came in below analyst estimates. Shares of Kioxia declined in Tokyo as investors digested the outlook.
24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.
The company attributed the soft outlook mainly to shipment timing, saying some orders were pulled into the September quarter while others were pushed into the March quarter. Chief Financial Officer Yoshihiko Kawamura said Kioxia expects a return to rapid growth in the March quarter. He added that AI data center demand remains robust and that Kioxia has sold out its planned output for next year.
Micron's slide also follows a weak prior session on October 30, when Samsung missed profit expectations. The open question for the group is whether Kioxia's outlook signals cooling AI memory demand and pricing, or whether the selling reflects broader tech positioning.
Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) stock is at $347.24, down 5%. That's a steeper decline than Micron's, making the hard drive maker the weakest of the three. During the past month, Western Digital has lost 24%. The company sells to hyperscalers, cloud service providers and enterprises building out storage for the AI-driven data economy.
SanDisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock is at $1,114.65, down 3%. The flash maker is falling less than Micron, which cuts against the idea that Kioxia's manufacturing partner would take the hardest hit. Across the past month, SanDisk has dropped 36%, the deepest decline in the group, and it declined in the prior session despite upbeat results reported on October 29.
Micron makes dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) along with NAND and NOR flash, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI systems. The company's Strategic Customer Agreements are designed to secure long-term demand visibility, particularly for AI workloads. This mix links Micron to both major memory markets at once.
Western Digital now operates as a hard disk drive company after separating its flash business into SanDisk, and it keeps an ownership interest in SanDisk. SanDisk, by contrast, designs and makes NAND flash and solid-state drives, producing wafers through Flash Ventures, its joint venture arrangements with Kioxia. That arrangement links SanDisk most directly to Kioxia's production, while Micron's DRAM exposure gives it pricing drivers that NAND-focused peers don't share.
Micron's upcoming earnings report will show whether pricing momentum holds up. On the September 30 call, President and Chief Operating Officer Manish Bhatia said Micron doesn't have "line of sight to when supply and demand balance." The company also noted it had "more than 75% of our shipments committed for the year." Kioxia's comments on order timing and sold-out output add support to that view.
Skeptics see a cycle nearing its peak. Analysts' average revenue estimate for Micron's fiscal year ending August 2027 is $275.5 billion, a high bar. Citrini Research analyst Jukan has read the sale of Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) to Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) as a sign that management expects the AI cycle to "collapse in two to three years," a view that remains one analyst's take.
Another weak stretch for the memory group could deepen Micron's monthly losses, while a pricing update matching Kioxia's upbeat March commentary could ease the pressure. A cautious approach may make sense until the memory-demand debate resolves.
